rows.col_1: GET https://developer.api.autodesk.com/construction/transmittals/v1/projects/{projectId}/transmittals
user context optional
data:read
JSON
Must be Bearer <token>, where <token> is obtained via either a two-legged or three-legged OAuth flow.

The Autodesk ID of the user on whose behalf the request is made.
This header is required only when using two-legged authentication. It is not needed for three-legged authentication.
Your application can access only those users who are assigned to it in the SaaS Integrations UI.
Only user Autodesk IDs (autodeskId) are supported.

The ID of the project.
You can retrieve the project ID using the Data Management API. For more details, see the Retrieve a Project ID tutorial.
You may provide the project ID with or without the b. prefix:

With prefix: b.657a5565-09b7-48e0-bd03-acacfe42efaf
Without prefix: 657a5565-09b7-48e0-bd03-acacfe42efaf

The maximum number of results to return per page.
Acceptable values: 1-200.
Default value: 20.
For example, to limit the response to two results per page, use limit=2.

The index from which the response starts returning results.
Default value: 0.
For example, to skip the first three results, use offset=3.

Sorts the transmittals by a supported field and order.

By default, results are sorted by sequenceId desc (descending order).
To sort in ascending order, add asc after the field name.
Format: sort=<field> [asc or desc]
Possible values: status, sequenceId, title, sentByName, createdAt, documentsCount.
Examples:

sort=status asc – sorts transmittals by status in ascending order.
sort=createdAt desc – sorts transmittals by creation date in descending order.

Successfully retrieved the list of transmittals
If one or more transmittals are still being processed, some fields—such as recipients and externalMembers—may be temporarily empty.
Bad request. The input parameters were invalid.
Unauthorized error
The user does not have permission to perform this operation.
The project does not exist
Internal server error
A list of transmittals that belong to the specified project.
The unique identifier of the transmittal.
A project-specific number automatically assigned when the transmittal is first submitted. It identifies the transmittal within the project and reflects the order in which it was created.
The title of the transmittal.
An optional message included with the transmittal.

The current processing state of the transmittal.

SENDING – The transmittal is being processed or packaged; some fields may be temporarily empty. The recipients and externalMembers fields may be temporarily empty.
COMPLETED – The transmittal has been successfully issued and all data is available.
FAILED – The transmittal failed to process or send.

Possible values: SENDING, COMPLETED, FAILED.
Information about the user who created and sent the transmittal.
The Autodesk ID of the transmittal creator.
The email of the transmittal creator.
The full name of the transmittal creator.
The Autodesk ID of the creator’s company at the time the transmittal was created.
The name of the creator’s company at the time the transmittal was created.

The list of recipients included in the transmittal, grouped by user, company, and role.
For more information on how to add recipients to a transmittal, see the Create Transmittals documentation.
The list of individual users who were added as recipients.
The Autodesk ID of the user recipient.
The name of the user recipient.
The list of companies that were added as recipients.
The Autodesk ID of the company recipient.
The name of the company recipient.
The list of project roles that were added as recipients.
The Autodesk ID of the role recipient.
The name of the role recipient.
The list of external recipients who are not members of the project.
The name of the external recipient.
The email address of the external recipient.
The date and time when the transmittal was created, in ISO 8601 format.
The total number of documents included in the transmittal.

Indicates the progress of packaging transmittal files into a ZIP archive.
Possible values: SUCCESS, PARTIAL_SUCCESS, FAILED, PROCESSING, EXPIRED, NOT_ALLOWED

Specifies how much recipient information each recipient can see.


ALL – All recipients can view the full recipient list.
LIMITED – Each recipient can view only their own recipient information.

Project Admins and the sender always see the full list.

Possible values: ALL, LIMITED
The list of pagination details for the response.
The maximum number of results returned per page.
The number of results skipped before the current page, starting from zero.
The total number of results that match the query, regardless of pagination.
The URL to retrieve the next page of transmittals. If this field is not included, the current page is the last page of results.
